summary: Iter 11 — Verified canonical onboarding HTTP layer + UI. Created /app/backend/tests/test_admin_onboarding_v2.py (15 tests, 13 PASS, 2 FAIL). All 4 verticals onboard correctly with lat/lng validation, pathology also spawns labs branch, approve-all gates on required docs then flips hospital_profiles+users to 'verified'. Geocode (OSM) returns results. Hospital migration endpoint returns {success,migrated}. Frontend AdminOnboarding form shows every requested data-testid, blocks hospital submit without coords (toast 'Latitude & longitude are required…'), and 'Look up from address' button geocodes Mumbai → 19.11,72.83. BLOCKER on patient detail: GET /api/admin/patients and /api/admin/patients/{id} return empty / 404 because the shared Supabase has ZERO users with role='patient' (verified: `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM users WHERE role='patient' = 0`), so the patient `3a60f23b-7b3e-4fc4-8437-26b4ff49b4e1` referenced in consultation_bookings has no identity row in public.users or auth.users. All test rows cleaned up at teardown.

critical.issue: list_all_patients_admin and fetch_patient_detail both hard-filter on `users.role='patient'`, but the shared Supabase has 0 rows with role='patient' (user_types in DB: provider_org, paramedic, individual, hospital_admin, ambulance_admin, pathologist). The specific patient_id `3a60f23b-7b3e-4fc4-8437-26b4ff49b4e1` referenced in `consultation_bookings` (Dr Jay, Fever) and `pathology_bookings` has NO row in public.users or auth.users. Result: admin roster is empty; patient detail returns 404; UI shows 'Patient unavailable / Patient not found'. Fix options: (a) seed a patient user row in public.users with role='patient' and id=3a60f23b-... matching the booking's patient_id, (b) relax fetch_patient_detail to accept users where role is NULL or user_type='individual', OR (c) derive the patient identity from consultation_bookings.patient_id (synthesize {id, name=null, phone=null}) when no users row exists so the appointments/lab_bookings still render.

integration_issues.issue: Page renders '[data-testid=patient-detail-error] Patient unavailable / Patient not found' because the backend returns 404 for the only live patient_id in consultation_bookings. UI itself is correct — this is strictly a backend data/filter issue.

rca of the issue: Patient detail 404 RCA: `fetch_patient_detail(user_id)` in supabase_db.py:1638-1644 does `SELECT role FROM public.users WHERE id=$1` and bails out with `return None` if `user is None OR user.role != 'patient'`. For the probe patient `3a60f23b-7b3e-4fc4-8437-26b4ff49b4e1`, `public.users` has NO row at all (user is None → return None → server.py:1722 raises 404). The patient_id lives only in child tables (consultation_bookings, pathology_bookings). Across the whole shared DB, `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM users WHERE role='patient' = 0` — all patient-app users must be using a different storage (likely auth.users which this project doesn't mirror, or a soft 'customer' role). Reproduction: `curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer <admin>' $BASE/api/admin/patients` → `{"patients":[],"total":0}`. Mitigation: in fetch_patient_detail, if no users row is found, synthesize `{id:user_id, name:null, phone:null}` and still return associations so the admin can at least see the Dr Jay / Fever booking + any lab bookings. Longer-term: create a 'patient' identity row in users whenever a consultation_bookings/pathology_bookings row is inserted (patient app side).
